overview:
A single Node.js process in three layers. The HTTP layer (Fastify) parses and validates requests and renders responses and errors. The service layer holds the rules: creating and resolving links, recording clicks, computing statistics. The data layer owns SQLite and is the only place that contains SQL. Dependencies point inwards only, and everything a layer needs is passed to it, so the whole application can be assembled in a test with an in-memory database, a fake clock and a scripted code generator.

The redirect is the hot path: one primary-key lookup, one in-memory push, one response. Click analytics are decoupled from it by a bounded in-memory queue that a timer writes in batches.

components.name: Configuration
components.responsibility: Read environment variables once, validate them, and fail startup on a bad value.

components.name: Database and migrator
components.responsibility: Open SQLite, run work in transactions, and apply numbered migrations exactly once with a stored checksum.

components.name: Domain rules
components.responsibility: Code generation, alias rules, destination URL rules, and the application error type.

components.name: Links
components.responsibility: Store and look up links; create with collision-safe code allocation.

components.name: Analytics
components.responsibility: Buffer click events and write them in batches; answer statistics queries.

components.name: HTTP
components.responsibility: Routes, request validation, rate limiting, problem-document errors, process lifecycle.

dataModelChanges: New table links(code primary key, target_url, created_at, click_count).
New table click_events(id, code references links, clicked_at, referrer_host) with an index on (code, clicked_at).
New table schema_migrations(version, checksum, applied_at), owned by the migrator.

decisions.title: Embedded SQLite through Node's built-in driver
decisions.decision: Store data in SQLite using node:sqlite, with all SQL confined to repository and analytics classes.
decisions.rationale: The requirement is a single command and no external services. The built-in driver needs no native build step, so installation cannot fail on a compiler or a blocked binary download. Confining SQL to two classes keeps a later move to a networked database local to them.
alternatives: PostgreSQL: the right choice for several instances, but it is an external service
better-sqlite3: mature, but a native module that must be compiled or downloaded at install time

decisions.title: Random codes, uniqueness enforced by the primary key
decisions.decision: Generate 7 random base62 characters from a cryptographic source, insert, and retry with a new code if the insert reports a clash, up to 5 times.
decisions.rationale: Random codes cannot be enumerated or guessed in sequence. Letting the primary key decide uniqueness removes the read-then-write race of checking first.
alternatives: Sequential counter encoded in base62: short, but every link is discoverable by counting
Hash of the URL: two callers shortening the same URL would share a code and its statistics

decisions.title: 302 with no-store for redirects
decisions.rationale: Click analytics is a requirement. A cached 301 means repeat visits never reach the service, and a link could never be changed or withdrawn later.
alternatives: 301: one request fewer for repeat visitors, at the cost of analytics and control

decisions.title: Click recording is asynchronous and best-effort
decisions.decision: A redirect pushes a click onto a bounded in-memory queue. A timer writes the queue in one transaction together with the per-link totals. When the queue is full, clicks are dropped and counted.
decisions.rationale: The requirement states that recording a click must never slow down or fail a redirect. A bounded queue keeps memory fixed under load, and one transaction per batch keeps the event rows and the totals consistent.
alternatives: Write synchronously in the redirect: exact counts, but a slow or locked database would slow or fail redirects
External message queue: durable, but an external service

decisions.title: Per-client token bucket on the management API only
decisions.decision: Rate limit /api/* per client address with an in-process token bucket whose key count is bounded. Redirects are not limited.
decisions.rationale: Link creation is the write an attacker can abuse; redirects are the product and are a single indexed read. The key bound stops a flood of distinct addresses from exhausting memory.
alternatives: Shared limiter in Redis: needed for several instances, but an external service
Limit redirects too: would throttle legitimate traffic to a popular link

decisions.title: Store the referrer's host only, and no client address
decisions.decision: Reduce the Referer header to its host before it is queued. Do not store or log the client address.
decisions.rationale: A full referrer URL can carry personal data in its path or query. Host-level data answers the stated question (top referrers) without holding personal data.
alternatives: Store the full referrer URL: more detail than was asked for, with a privacy cost

decisions.title: Errors as RFC 9457 problem documents
decisions.decision: Every error response is application/problem+json with a stable machine-readable code. Unexpected errors are logged in full and returned as a generic 500.
decisions.rationale: Clients get one error shape to handle, and internal detail never leaves the process.
alternatives: Ad-hoc JSON error bodies per route

decisions.title: Run the TypeScript sources directly
decisions.decision: Use Node's built-in type stripping; type-check with tsc --noEmit as a separate step.
decisions.rationale: No build output to keep in sync and a single start command. The cost is a minimum Node version of 22.18 and a restriction to erasable TypeScript syntax, which the compiler enforces.
alternatives: Compile to dist/ with tsc: works on older Node versions, adds a build step
tsx or ts-node: an extra runtime dependency

risks.risk: The API has no authentication, so anyone who can reach it can create links and read statistics.
risks.mitigation: Rate limiting on the management API, and deployment behind a trusted gateway. Authentication is listed as out of scope and as a known limitation.

risks.risk: Clicks still in the queue when the process stops are lost.
risks.mitigation: Accepted for this version under the best-effort assumption A-2 and documented as a limitation. Flushing on shutdown is the follow-up.

risks.risk: A shortener is an open redirector and can be used to disguise malicious destinations.
risks.mitigation: Only http and https, no embedded credentials, no self-reference. Destination reputation checks are out of scope and recorded as a follow-up.

risks.risk: SQLite and in-process limiter state do not support more than one instance.
risks.mitigation: Recorded as assumption A-1. SQL is confined to the data layer so the store can be replaced.

risks.risk: node:sqlite is still marked experimental and its API may change.
risks.mitigation: Pinned minimum Node version, a lock file, and the driver hidden behind the data layer.
Daily statistics read only a 30-day window through an index. A retention job is a follow-up.

requirementCoverage.how: LinkService.create validates the URL and alias with the domain rules and allocates a code by insert-and-retry on the primary key.
GET /{code} looks the link up by primary key and replies 302 with no-store.
ClickRecorder writes events and totals; StatsService reads the total, a 30-day per-day breakdown and the top 10 referrer hosts.
An onRequest hook applies a per-client token bucket to /api/* and raises 429 with Retry-After.
The redirect only pushes to a bounded queue; batches are written by a timer in one transaction.
/healthz always answers; /readyz runs a trivial query and answers 503 if it fails.
One error handler renders AppError and framework 4xx errors as problem documents and everything else as a generic 500.
